papers.title: Inductive Biases in Field-Level Cosmological Inference from Galaxy Catalogs
papers.comment: 23 pages, 8 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal
papers.summary: Deep Sets and graph neural networks infer Ωm from simulated CAMELS galaxy catalogs; graph models reach ~10% error, with peculiar velocities dominating set-based inference.
papers.tldr: Results indicate that peculiar velocities provide the dominant source of Ωm information for set-based models in this setting, while spatial information is most effectively used by architectures that explicitly encode galaxy–galaxy relations.

papers.title: A Machine Learning Approach to Coupling Photoionization & Multi-Frequency Radiation Hydrodynamics
papers.summary: Random forest models trained on XSTAR outputs predict line-driving force multipliers for Athena++ radiation hydrodynamics, outperforming trilinear interpolation across ionization, optical depth, and SED temperature.
papers.tldr: This work finds that random forest models provide the highest accuracy and reproduce the force multipliers over a three-dimensional parameter space more accurately, and with less training data, than traditional precomputed tables using trilinear interpolation.

papers.title: MP-DualNet: A Dual-Branch Deep Learning Approach for Magnetopause Boundary Detection Using Simulated SXI Images
papers.summary: MP-DualNet, a dual-branch deep learning model, detects magnetopause boundaries in simulated SXI images, achieving >0.94 classification accuracy and >0.97 segmentation IoU.
papers.tldr: MP‐DualNet is developed, an end‐to‐end dual‐branch deep learning framework for automated magnetopause detection from simulated SXI observations that maintains robust performance across a wide range of noise levels and generalizes well, as demonstrated by its application to an independent storm event.

papers.title: Survey of Surveys Data Release 3. Homogenised stellar parameters across nine spectroscopic surveys
papers.comment: Submitted to A&A. 20 pages, 17 figures, 5 tables
papers.summary: Machine-learning regression homogenises effective temperature, surface gravity, and metallicity across nine spectroscopic surveys, producing a 10.13-million-star catalogue with reduced survey offsets.
